introduction: This level analyzes the strategic conflicts within these blocs, efforts to challenge the US Dollar, and India's major trade policy decisions.

core_concepts.title: De-dollarization
core_concepts.description: A major undeclared goal of BRICS is to reduce the dominance of the US Dollar in global trade. Members are increasingly using 'Local Currencies' (e.g., Rupee-Rouble trade) and discussing the creation of a 'Shared BRICS Currency' for settlements.

core_concepts.title: RCEP (Regional Comprehensive Economic Partnership)
core_concepts.description: The world's largest Free Trade Agreement (FTA) between ASEAN (10 nations) and 5 of its FTA partners (China, Japan, South Korea, Australia, New Zealand).

core_concepts.title: India's Exit from RCEP (2019)
core_concepts.description: India was part of the RCEP negotiations but pulled out in 2019. Reason: India feared that signing RCEP would flood the Indian market with 'Cheap Chinese Goods' and 'Dairy Products' from New Zealand/Australia, destroying local farmers and MSMEs.

core_concepts.title: Voice of the Global South
core_concepts.description: In G20 and BRICS, India is positioning itself as the leader of the 'Global South' (developing and poor nations). India aims to ensure that Western powers (G7) do not impose their climate or economic rules on developing countries.

important_entities.name: Decline of SAARC and Rise of BIMSTEC
important_entities.significance: Due to India-Pakistan tensions, SAARC is effectively dead. India has shifted its focus to 'BIMSTEC' (Bay of Bengal Initiative), which excludes Pakistan but includes other neighbors like Thailand and Myanmar.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: Remember that all G7 members (US, UK, Canada, France, Germany, Italy, Japan) are part of the G20. However, India, China, and Russia are NOT part of the G7.

mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: BIMSTEC is centered around the Bay of Bengal, where Pakistan has no coastline. This helps you remember that Pakistan is not a member.

exam_strategy_tips: For UPSC Mains, 'Why did India opt-out of RCEP?' and 'Can BRICS be a real alternative to the World Bank/IMF?' are essential analytical topics.
